name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,420

clue.text: A panel of judges trying to eat a cake

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: a trial is the trying of a case in court
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A bench of judges hearing a case over a cake, as if the cake were in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A panel of judges' looks like the subject of the sentence; 'trying' is a noun in disguise, a court trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body appointed to adjudicate disputes, typically sitting as a group of legal officials.

clue.text: Office worker is endlessly kind - and is on time

indicators.note: without its end, the word for kind loses its final letter

blocks.note: a type is a kind; its last letter goes
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A kindly office worker who is always punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: TYPE loses its E, then IS sits on T; 'on' in a down clue means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist is a clerical employee whose job is keying letters and documents, a classic office role.

clue.text: The top parts of it could easily conceal Arctic permafrost

definitions.text: The top parts of it could easily conceal Arctic permafrost

indicators.note: the top of each word in a down clue is its first letter, so only the leading letters count

blocks.clueFragment: it could easily conceal Arctic permafrost
blocks.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A remark about frozen ground lying hidden beneath a polar covering.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the first letters spell ICECAP, and an ice cap is the frozen top that would hide the ground beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice covering polar land, sitting on top of the frozen ground below.

clue.text: Peacekeepers' help is not delivered

blocks.note: the UN supplies peacekeeping forces; the apostrophe adds the possessive S
aid means help

explanation.surface: Aid promised by UN peacekeepers fails to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Peacekeepers' help reads as UN'S AID, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Words left unsaid were never spoken, just as a speech not delivered is never voiced aloud.

clue.text: A firm on St Lucia working without electricity?

indicators.note: the place name is put to work and its letters rearranged into fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
letters of the Caribbean island's name

explanation.surface: A business based on the Caribbean island coping with a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: an acoustic guitar is played unplugged.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustical instruments make sound naturally rather than through amplification, so they need no mains power or amplifier.

clue.text: Bits of green veg and small green fruit

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
pears are a common orchard fruit

explanation.surface: A list of green produce: vegetables and some unripe fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' appears twice; the second one is only colour for the pears and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus and broccoli are sold as spears, the long edible shoots of these green vegetables.

clue.text: Picture of Dad (and not a Mum)

blocks.note: pa is a word for father
nor means and not
taken as written
ma is a word for mother

explanation.surface: A photograph showing father alone, with mother left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide view or picture of a broad scene, such as a sweeping landscape photograph.

clue.text: Turn away foreigner at entrance to embassy

indicators.note: the entrance is the way in, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: an alien is a foreigner
taken as written
the first letter of embassy

explanation.surface: A foreign visitor being refused admission at an embassy door.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to estrange them, pushing them away so they become hostile or unfriendly.

clue.text: Beach 'shoes' are flip-flops!

indicators.note: to flip-flop is to keep changing about, so the letters before it turn over into another order

blocks.note: letters of the word in quotes
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A wry note that the only footwear people wear at the beach is flip-flops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is part of the fodder as well as the verb: SHOES plus ARE, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A seashore is the strip of land beside the sea, which is just what a beach is.

clue.text: The place from which sports reporters watch crowd fight

definitions.text: The place from which sports reporters watch

blocks.note: to press is to crowd, and a press is a crowd
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Journalists at a match look on as spectators start brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: A press box is the reserved enclosure at a stadium where journalists sit to cover the game.

clue.text: Chest complaint treated again with nitrates, primarily

indicators.note: something treated is processed and changed, so these letters are worked into a new order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of nitrates

explanation.surface: A heart patient's pain being treated once more with nitrate drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Nitrates such as nitroglycerin really are the standard treatment, which makes the surface accurate medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle.

clue.text: Most terrifying racists struggling to grasp English

indicators.note: people struggling are thrown about, so the letters here are scrambled
to grasp something is to hold it inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: letters taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Bigots having trouble with the English language are the most frightening sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Scariest is the superlative of scary, meaning causing the greatest fear.

clue.text: Cut right into fish

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An instruction to slice straight into a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' is a noun here: a trench is a cut dug in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow excavation, a cut made into the earth.

clue.text: Fight, or quickly drop to the ground for cover

indicators.note: the long phrase acts as cover, wrapping round the small word placed inside it

blocks.note: free fall is a fast unchecked drop earthwards
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice when a brawl breaks out: hit the deck and take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link between definition and wordplay, but it is the fodder that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorderly brawl or contest in which anyone may join in.

clue.text: It accurately measures organised computer crime without using CPU

indicators.note: organised means arranged anew, so these letters are put into a different order
doing without some letters means they are dropped from the fodder

blocks.note: letters taken as written
these three letters are removed

explanation.surface: Organised cybercrime that avoids using a central processing unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one C, the P and the U from COMPUTER CRIME, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A micrometer is a precision gauge used to measure tiny thicknesses and diameters very exactly.

clue.text: Out of sight of the house, kill an animal with butt of rifle

definitions.text: Out of sight of the house

indicators.note: the butt is the end of a rifle, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: to off someone is slang for to kill
a stag is a male deer
the last letter of rifle

explanation.surface: A hunter on an estate, out of view of the manor, shooting game with a rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is the theatre audience, not a country home.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage means behind the scenes, where the theatre audience in the auditorium cannot see.

clue.text: Various addicts extremely well equipped with drugs

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are taken

blocks.note: the first and last letters of addicts
sorted is British slang for supplied with what you need, especially drugs

explanation.surface: Drug users with a plentiful stash of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of mixed kinds, a selection of different sorts.

clue.text: Criminal tried taking in soldiers, resulting in tragedy

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the next word's letters are twisted
taking something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: letters taken as written
the SAS is the British special forces regiment

explanation.surface: A crook put on trial after taking soldiers captive, ending in catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a sudden event causing great loss or suffering.

clue.text: Drunken teens principally dance as if spellbound

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order
principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of teens
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tipsy teenagers on the dance floor, moving as though in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Fascinated means utterly captivated, held as if under a spell, unable to look away.

clue.text: Lucky charm bringing millions to Andy Murray?

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for million
the tennis player is a Scot, so he is A SCOT

explanation.surface: A talisman that earns the tennis star a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Murray is a Scottish tennis champion; the clue wants a description of him, not his sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object believed to bring good luck to a team or person.

clue.text: It's fairly rude, and I go red outwardly

indicators.note: acting outwardly means being on the outside, wrapping around the letter

blocks.note: to blush is to go red in the face
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits a joke is a bit risqué and they are embarrassed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue means smutty or risqué, so somewhat blue is fairly rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are indecent ones, so a bluish remark is mildly off-colour or somewhat risqué.

clue.text: Angry scientist portrayed by Aussie actor in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: Eric Bana is the Australian actor who played the role in the 2003 film Hulk

explanation.surface: An Australian actor trying out for the part of a furious scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce Banner is the scientist who turns into the Hulk when angry; in a non-rhotic accent BANNER and Bana sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce Banner is the Marvel physicist whose rage transforms him into the Incredible Hulk.

clue.text: Work hard to introduce a new catchphrase

blocks.note: to slog is to work hard
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An advertising team toiling to launch a fresh tagline.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable motto or phrase used in advertising or politics.

clue.text: Company - possibly Apple - initially agrees to take a lesser charge

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements of the letters
initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
letters taken as written
the first letter of agrees

explanation.surface: A tech giant settling a legal case by accepting a reduced charge.
explanation.walkthrough: To cop a plea is a mainly American idiom for pleading guilty to a lesser offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Copping a plea means pleading guilty to a lesser offence to avoid trial on a more serious one.

clue.text: Canny, like someone learning to finish early

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping before the last letter, which is cut off

blocks.note: as means like
a tutee is someone being taught; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A shrewd student who wraps up lessons ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means sharp and shrewd, quick to judge situations to one's advantage.

clue.text: A penalty is OK

definitions.note: the article goes with the noun: a penalty is a sanction

blocks.note: first meaning: a punishment imposed for breaking a rule
second meaning: as a verb, to approve or authorise

explanation.walkthrough: The word is its own opposite: it can mean both a punishment and a permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanction can mean a punitive measure such as trade restrictions, and also to give official approval.

clue.text: Bear dying alongside a river

blocks.note: death is one's end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A bear perishing on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is a verb, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate or put up with it, exactly as enduring does.

clue.text: One getting infiltrated by large weapons manufacturer

indicators.note: something infiltrated has an intruder slipped inside it

blocks.note: a fetcher is one who goes to get things
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An arms maker whose firm has been penetrated by a big spy operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One getting' together means someone who gets things, a fetcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher is a maker of arrows, a craftsman who manufactures weapons for archers.
